task.question: What age was the graffiti artist HRH Helch when he passed away?
task.evidence: He was only 34, which almost doesn’t make sense. It feels like his work has been around for ever, as much a part of the British urban landscape as red phone boxes and uncollected bins. In a post on Instagram, his gallery, BSMT Space, said “an urban landscape without an H in it seems unfathomable”. And it’s true, that towering letter defined the look of late 2010s Britain.
task.page: HRH Helch: the graffiti artist who left an indelible mark on high-rise Britain

[Helch] Helch (1991 or 1992 – August 2026), often stylised as HELCH, was the tag of a pseudonymous graffiti artist, who operated mainly in the United Kingdom, and was known for his stylised capital lettering. Brought up in Hayes, Hillingdon, Helch first came to public prominence in 2018 with his alteration of the "give peas a chance" graffiti on the Chalfont Viaduct over the M25 to "helch: a chance taken" and later "give helch a break". The Helch tag later spread across walls and rooftoops across the globe, in increasingly stylised forms in a range of colours, either alone, or as a wider set of slogans, or sometimes just as an ornate letter 'H'. On 29 August 2026, Helch was reported to have died, aged 34. He was widely regarded as "The Roller King" within the art community due to his iconic tag being created using a roller. The art gallery he partnered with, BSMT, confirmed his death and paid tribute to him the following day.
